It ran from February 7 to December 12. [[Club Sport Emelec|Emelec]] and [[Liga Deportiva Universitaria de Quito|LDU Quito]] each won the First and Second Stage, respectively, and played each other in the [[#Finals|championship finals]]. LDU Quito won the first leg at home by a score of 2–0. Emelec could not overturn the deficit with a 1–0 win at home in the second leg. LDU Quito won their tenth national title, tying them for third overall with Emelec. ==Format== A new format for the 2010 season was announced by the [[Ecuadorian Football Federation]] on December 15, 2009.{{cite web |url=http://www.ecuafutbol.org/UI/detalle.aspx?seccion=1&categserie=7&nivel=0&subnivel=0&id=15807&tabla=N |title=La FEF definió el sistema de Campeonato para 2010 |language=es |trans-title=FEF defined the format for 2010 |work=Website |publisher=[[Ecuadorian Football Federation]] |access-date=December 16, 2009 |year=2009 |archive-date=April 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200404231411/http://www.ecuafutbol.org/UI/detalle.aspx?seccion=1&categserie=7&nivel=0&subnivel=0&id=15807&tabla=N |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.futbolecuador.com/stories/publica/11767 |title=Se ratificó el Sistema de Campeonato de la A |language=es |trans-title=They ratified the format of the Serie A |date=January 8, 2010 |access-date=January 8, 2010 |work=website |publisher=futbolecuador.com }} The season was divided into three stages. The First and Second Stages were identical stages with a double round-robin format. Each team played the others twice, once at home and once away. The winners of each stage qualified to play a two-legged tie in the Third Stage for the title. The two highest non-stage winners in the aggregate table of the First and Second Stages played each in another two-legged tie in a Third Stage playoff for third place. Had the same team won both stages, they would have been automatically be crowned the champion. In that case, a two-legged tie would have been held in the Third Stage between the two best-placed teams in the aggregate table to determine who is the runner-up and who finished in third place. The two teams at the bottom of the aggregate table of the first two stages were relegated to the Serie B for the following season. ===International qualification=== The two stage winners earned a berth to the [[2011 Copa Libertadores]]. The berth ''Ecuador 1'' went to the champion, ''Ecuador 2'' went to the runner-up, and ''Ecuador 3'' went to the third-place finisher. Teams also qualified to two [[Copa Sudamericana]]s. The top-three teams in the First Stage qualified to the [[2010 Copa Sudamericana]] (except [[Liga Deportiva Universitaria de Quito|LDU Quito]], who had a berth as the [[2009 Copa Sudamericana|defending Copa Sudamericana champion]]). The winner of the Second Stage earned the ''Ecuador 1'' berth for the [[2011 Copa Sudamericana]]. ==Teams== Twelve teams competed in the 2010 Serie A season, ten of whom remained from the 2009 season. [[Liga Deportiva Universitaria de Portoviejo|LDU Portoviejo]] and [[Club Deportivo Técnico Universitario|Técnico Universitario]] were relegated last season to the Serie B after accumulating the fewest points in the [[2009 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A#Aggregate table|First and Second Stage aggregate table]]. They were replaced by [[Club Social y Deportivo Independiente José Terán|Independiente José Terán]]{{cite news |url=http://www.elcomercio.com/Generales/Solo-Texto.aspx?gn3articleID=167584 |title=Independiente del Valle se clasificó a la A |language=es |trans-title=Independiente del Valle classified to the A |date=October 8, 2010 |access-date=May 17, 2010 |newspaper=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]] }} and [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica del Ecuador|Universidad Católica]],{{cite news |url=http://www.elcomercio.com/Generales/Solo-Texto.aspx?gn3articleID=166349 |title=Católica ascendió a la Serie A y hundió a Aucas en el fondo de la tabla |language=es |trans-title=Católica ascended to the Serie A and sunk Aucas at the bottom of the table |date=October 4, 2010 |access-date=May 17, 2010 |newspaper=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]] }} the 2009 Serie B winner and runner-up, respectively.{{cite news |url=http://www.elcomercio.com/Generales/Solo-Texto.aspx?gn3articleID=167587 |title=Independiente se coronó campeón con una goleada |language=es |trans-title=Independiente was crowned the champion with a heavy defeat |date=October 26, 2009 |access-date=May 17, 2010 |newspaper=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]] }} This was Universidad Católica's 27th season in the Serie A, having last played in the league in [[2008 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A|2008]]. This was Independiente José Terán's first season in the Serie A. One team used a different stadium this season.
